title: PRD: Tiered actionability matrix and triggered remediation for Optimize evals
creator: Priya Desai
description: Problem: Optimize needs a deterministic, actionable policy that maps composite eval signals to concrete remediation actions during staged rollouts. Current eval alerts are noisy and often require manual triage. This PRD defines a tiered actionability matrix that ranks signals by severity and confidence, specifies statistical tests and minimum sample sizes for A/B canaries, and prescribes automatic and operator-driven remediation steps (pause, rollback, partial throttle, degrade to fallback model). The goal is to reduce time-to-remediation, avoid unnecessary rollbacks, and provide clear escalation paths for ambiguous regressions.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A tiered actionability matrix exists (Low/Medium/High) that maps at least six composite signal classes to a default remediation action.
A2: Statistical test suite implemented: two-sided bootstrap and permutation tests available in the eval pipeline with configurable alpha; default alpha set to 0.01 for High-severity signals.

A3: Minimum sample sizing logic implemented so canary runs enforce required sample sizes per metric and cohort before any automated remediation triggers (sample size calculator documented and integrated into Dashboard).
A4: Canary policy implemented: canary stages (1%, 5%, 25%), automated gate checks at each stage, with pause-on-failure and automatic rollback rules for High severity signals.
A5: Signal hierarchy implemented so Safety/Toxicity/hallucination regressions supersede throughput/cost regressions when conflicting signals appear during a rollout.
A6: An operator-visible runbook is linked from the Dashboard with clickable actions (Pause, Rollback, Throttle, Open Incident) and each action records rationale in audit logs.
A7: End-to-end QA: synthetic prompt-set injection tests reproduce a known regression and trigger the expected High-tier remediation in an instrumented staging rollout.
A8: Release notes and handoff docs completed for SRE and Support with 1-hour response SLAs for High-tier alerts for the first two weeks after launch.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal validation — run matrix locally against standard Optimize prompt-sets and historical baselines (Mar 9–12).
Phase 1: Instrumented canary to 1% traffic for two days, require metric stability and sample counts before progressing (Mar 15–16).
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 5% and 25%, with automated gating at each step (Mar 17–21).
Phase 3: Full rollout contingent on zero High-tier automated remediations and <0.5% medium-tier manual interventions during ramp (target complete Mar 28).
Rollback criteria are codified in the matrix and automatically executed when threshold and test conditions are met.
monitoring_signals: Primary Quality: Accuracy delta (task-specific) relative to baseline
Safety: Toxicity score increase (TOX-avg) and worst-case cohort spikes
Hallucination: Factuality regression measured by reference-based metrics and human-annotated golden prompts
Throughput: tokens/sec under typical request distribution
Customer-facing error rate: HTTP 5xx and model timeouts
Composite signals: weighted aggregate (weights configurable) used for initial triage
statistical_tests: Default tests: two-sided bootstrap for metric deltas with 10k resamples
Sequential analysis guard: use alpha-spending function for staged rollouts to control type I error across multiple looks
Minimum detectable effect (MDE) requirement per metric computed and enforced prior to claiming a regression
False positive control: require both statistical significance (p < alpha) AND practical significance (absolute delta > effect_threshold) for automatic High-tier actions
